name: Gmail
summary: Difficulty depends almost entirely on which Gmail scope you need. Sending mail needs Google's review, but reading mail for public users uses restricted scopes, which take weeks of review and a yearly third-party security assessment.
biggestRisk: An agent that reads email needs restricted scopes such as gmail.readonly, so plan for a security assessment before public launch.

paths.name: Test with up to 100 named users
paths.whenToUse: You're building or running a pilot with people you can list by email.

wait.note: No approval step on this path.

steps.title: Decide the exact Gmail scopes
steps.detail: Map each agent action to the narrowest scope. This decides which path you end up on, so do it first.
steps.confirm: Each scope is labeled sensitive or restricted in your notes.

steps.title: Create a project and consent screen
steps.detail: In Google Cloud Console, create a project, enable the Gmail API, set the audience to External and leave the status as Testing. Add your test users.
steps.confirm: Test users are listed under the app's audience settings.
steps.handoffReason: This requires your Google account and accepting Google's terms.

steps.title: Create a web OAuth client
steps.detail: Create a Web application client and add the redirect URI from your Composio auth config.
steps.confirm: A test user connects and sees the unverified-app warning, which is expected.

blockers.symptom: Connections stop working after a week
blockers.cause: External apps in Testing get refresh tokens that expire in 7 days unless they only use basic identity scopes.
blockers.action: Reconnect during testing, and don't treat this as a bug in your integration. It goes away once the app is in production.

paths.name: Internal to your organization
paths.whenToUse: Everyone who will connect is in your own Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization.

wait.note: No approval step on this path.

steps.title: Set the user type to Internal
steps.detail: Follow the testing setup, but choose Internal as the audience. This requires a project inside your organization.
steps.confirm: Colleagues can connect without an unverified-app warning.
steps.handoffReason: This requires an account in that organization.

blockers.symptom: Internal isn't offered as an option
blockers.cause: Internal needs a project in a Workspace or Cloud Identity organization. A personal Gmail account doesn't have one.
blockers.action: Create the project under your organization, or use the testing path.

paths.name: Public launch, sending only
paths.whenToUse: Your agent sends email for any user but doesn't need to read their mailbox.

wait.note: Brand verification typically takes 2 to 3 business days. We found no stated time for sensitive-scope review, and a resubmission would extend it.

steps.title: Prepare your public pages
steps.detail: Draft a home page and a privacy policy that describes your Gmail data use, on the same domain.
steps.confirm: Both pages load publicly without sign-in on the domain you'll verify.

steps.title: Verify your domain
steps.detail: Verify ownership in Google Search Console with an account that's an Owner or Editor on the project.
steps.confirm: Search Console shows the domain as verified.
steps.handoffReason: This requires DNS or site access.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Show the consent flow with your app name and client ID visible, then show what each scope does. Upload it as Unlisted on YouTube.
steps.confirm: The client ID is readable in the browser address bar on the video.
steps.handoffReason: It has to show your real, running product.

steps.title: Submit for verification and wait
steps.detail: Submit from the Cloud Console and watch the project's contact email closely for questions.
steps.confirm: The console shows the app as verified.

blockers.symptom: Google asks you to justify a scope
blockers.cause: Apps must request only the least privilege their features need.
blockers.action: Show each scope in use in the video, and drop any scope you can't show.

paths.name: Public launch, reading mail
paths.whenToUse: Your agent reads, modifies or manages mail for users outside your organization.

wait.note: Google says only that review can take several weeks. The range is our estimate and includes assessor time, which we couldn't source.

steps.title: Check you're a permitted application type
steps.detail: Compare your product against Google's Limited Use and permitted app types before spending anything else. A general assistant may not qualify automatically.
steps.confirm: You can name the permitted category your product falls into.

steps.title: Complete everything on the sending path
steps.detail: Public pages, domain verification and the demo video are all still required. Task automation platforms must also show how API workflows are created and where user data flows.
steps.handoffReason: These need your domain and running product.

steps.title: Pass the security assessment
steps.detail: Engage a Google-approved assessor and fix what they find. The agent can help prepare evidence, but you own the remediation.
steps.confirm: The assessor issues a Letter of Assessment.
steps.handoffReason: An independent assessor has to evaluate your systems.

steps.title: Wait for Google's review
steps.detail: Respond quickly to any follow-up questions, then publish within the 7-day validity window of your results.
steps.confirm: The console shows the app as verified.

blockers.symptom: Access is threatened 12 months after approval
blockers.cause: Reverification is required at least every 12 months.
blockers.action: Put the renewal on your calendar and keep project contacts current, as Google emails those addresses.

nuances.title: Composio's app may remove this work
nuances.detail: Gmail is listed as managed, so you could use Composio's app and skip registration while your users see Composio's name. We couldn't confirm which scopes it's approved for, so check them against your needs.

nuances.title: Changing a password can break the connection
nuances.detail: Tokens with Gmail scopes can stop working when a user changes their password. Your agent should handle this by asking the user to reconnect.

nuances.title: Token limit in testing
nuances.detail: Each Google Account can hold 100 refresh tokens per OAuth client, and the oldest is silently invalidated beyond that. Heavy reconnect testing can hit this.
